'''Amit Chakrabarti''' (born November 11, 1959) is the former William and Joan Porter Chair in Physics at [[Kansas State University]].<ref>Amit Chakrabarti's curriculum vitae:http://www.phys.ksu.edu/personal/amitc/Amit_Chakrabarti_wiki_CV_2013.pdf</ref> He currently serves as the dean of the college of arts and sciences at [[Kansas State University]].

Chakrabarti is a [[theoretical physicist]] with interests in [[soft matter]] and [[statistical physics]]. He has worked on diverse soft matter systems, including [[liquid]] [[mixtures]], [[polymers]], [[liquid crystals]], [[aerosols]], [[colloids]], [[nanoparticles]], and most recently, [[self-assembly]] of [[proteins]].<ref>Amit Chakrabarti's Media Bio: http://www.k-state.edu/media/mediaguide/bios/chakrabartibio.html</ref>

==Biography==
Chakrabarti was born in [[Calcutta, India]]. He earned his [[Bachelor of Science]] in physics in 1979 and [[Master of Science]] in [[physics]] in 1982 from the [[University of Calcutta]], and earned his [[doctorate]] in [[physics]] from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1987. He was a [[research associate]] at [[Temple University]] from 1987 to 1988 and  at [[Lehigh University]] from 1988 to 1989.

Chakrabarti joined the [[physics]] department at [[Kansas State University]] in 1990 and was named a full professor in 2000. He served as interim head of the department of physics from 2006 to 2007. In July 2011, Chakrabarti was named the William and Joan Porter Chair in Physics.

==Academics and research==
Chakrabarti's research   focuses on how [[particles]] in a dispersed phase come together and form [[aggregate (composite)|aggregate]]s. His individual and collaborative research projects have received extramural funding from agencies such as [[NASA]] and the [[National Science Foundation]]. He has published more than 150 peer-reviewed papers and mentored nine doctoral students and several postdoctoral fellows.

Chakrabarti and co-workers'   numerical work in the late 1980s settled a long-standing controversy on the value of domain growth exponent in quenched far from equilibrium systems.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Chakrabarti | first1=Amitabha | last2=Toral | first2=Raúl | last3=Gunton | first3=James D. | title=Late stages of spinodal decomposition in a three-dimensional model system | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=39 | issue=7 | date=1989-03-01 | issn=0163-1829 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.39.4386 | pages=4386–4394| pmid=9948781 | bibcode=1989PhRvB..39.4386C }}</ref> He carried out large-scale [[simulations]] of [[conformational isomerism|conformations]] of grafted chains<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Chakrabarti | first1=Amitabha | last2=Toral | first2=Raul | title=Density profile of terminally anchored polymer chains: a Monte Carlo study | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=23 | issue=7 | year=1990 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma00209a023 | pages=2016–2021| bibcode=1990MaMol..23.2016C }}</ref> that prompted several detailed experiments on this subject. He is a co-author of the first [[simulation]] work<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brown | first1=Gregory | last2=Chakrabarti | first2=Amitabha | title=Surface-directed spinodal decomposition in a two-dimensional model | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=46 | issue=8 | date=1992-10-01 | issn=1050-2947 | doi=10.1103/physreva.46.4829 | pages=4829–4835| pmid=9908702 | bibcode=1992PhRvA..46.4829B }}</ref> on how selective surface interactions influence [[spinodal decomposition]] in a mixture. This paper led to a flurry of experimental activities and confirmation of his groups' theoretical findings.

His work on [[phase (matter)|phase]] separation in [[fluids]] with long-chain molecules<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bhattacharya | first1=Aniket | last2=Mahanti | first2=S. D. | last3=Chakrabarti | first3=Amitabha | title=Networklike Pattern Formation in Phase Separating Polymer Solutions: A Molecular Dynamics Study | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=80 | issue=2 | date=1998-01-12 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.80.333 | pages=333–336| bibcode=1998PhRvL..80..333B }}</ref> explained why different experiments carried out to different time regimes seem to produce contradictory results. His group's large-scale [[simulation]] on aggregation [[kinetics (physics)|kinetics]] in [[Particle density (packed density)|dense]] [[particulate]] systems<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Fry | first1=D. | last2=Sintes | first2=Tomàs | last3=Chakrabarti | first3=A. | last4=Sorensen | first4=C. M. | title=Enhanced Kinetics and Free-Volume Universality in Dense Aggregating Systems | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=89 | issue=14 | date=2002-09-10 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.89.148301 | article-number=148301| pmid=12366078 | bibcode=2002PhRvL..89n8301F | hdl=10261/15299 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> explained Christopher Sorensen's research group's experimental observation of speed up in the kinetics of aggregation in a dense system and developed the concept of [[cluster (physics)|cluster]] crowding in aggregating systems. Chakrabarti and Christopher Sorensen, Cortelyou-Rust University Distinguished Professor of physics at Kansas State University, have published a recent invited review<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Sorensen | first1=C. M. | last2=Chakrabarti | first2=A. | title=The sol to gel transition in irreversible particulate systems | journal=Soft Matter | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=7 | issue=6 | year=2011 | issn=1744-683X | doi=10.1039/c0sm00228c | pages=2284–2296| bibcode=2011SMat....7.2284S }}</ref> that provides a comprehensive description of their research of how a system of [[particles]] evolves from a dilute [[sol (colloid)|sol]] to a [[gel]]. This paper identifies new regimes of aggregation.

His research group has developed a [[phenomenology (particle physics)|phenomenological]] model for [[Chemical reaction|interactions]] among [[Chemical ligation|ligated]] [[gold nanoparticles]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Khan | first1=Siddique J. | last2=Pierce | first2=F. | last3=Sorensen | first3=C. M. | last4=Chakrabarti | first4=A. | title=Self-Assembly of Ligated Gold Nanoparticles: Phenomenological Modeling and Computer Simulations | journal=Langmuir | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=25 | issue=24 | date=2009-12-15 | issn=0743-7463 | doi=10.1021/la9008202 | pages=13861–13868| pmid=19441832 }}</ref> based on a [[Physical model|model]] of grafted [[polymer]] chains.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Chakrabarti | first1=Amitabha | last2=Toral | first2=Raul | title=Density profile of terminally anchored polymer chains: a Monte Carlo study | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=23 | issue=7 | year=1990 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma00209a023 | pages=2016–2021| bibcode=1990MaMol..23.2016C }}</ref> This work successfully explained Christopher Sorensen's research group's experimentally observed values for the [[superlattice]] constants for [[gold nanoparticles]] decorated with various ligands and the trend in [[solubility]] of nanoparticles seen in experiments.

Chakrabarti's research group is currently carrying out [[simulation]] study of [[nanoparticle]] [[supercluster]] [[nucleation]]. Analysis of a pre-[[nucleation]] [[induction period]] yielded a [[supercluster]] interfacial [[tension (physics)|tensions]] that compare reasonably well with other theory and Christopher Sorensen's research group's experiments.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Khan | first1=Siddique J. | last2=Sorensen | first2=C. M. | last3=Chakrabarti | first3=A. | title=Computer Simulations of Nucleation of Nanoparticle Superclusters from Solution | journal=Langmuir | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=28 | issue=13 | date=2012-03-19 | issn=0743-7463 | doi=10.1021/la2050306 | pages=5570–5579| pmid=22385301 }}</ref> This work also suggests that the [[nucleation]] process for ligated [[nanoparticles]] is a two-step process as seen in some  protein   nucleation  studies.

In collaboration with James Gunton,  professor of  physics  at [[Lehigh University]],<ref>James D. Gunton: http://www.lehigh.edu/~jdg4/</ref> one of Chakrabarti's recent projects focuses<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Wei | last2=Gunton | first2=J. D. | last3=Khan | first3=Siddique J. | last4=Schoelz | first4=J. K. | last5=Chakrabarti | first5=A. | title=Brownian dynamics simulation of insulin microsphere formation from break-up of a fractal network | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=134 | issue=2 | date=2011-01-14 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.3517865 | page=024902| pmid=21241148 | bibcode=2011JChPh.134b4902L }}</ref> on understanding how [[insulin]] [[crystals]] form from [[aqueous solutions]].  . His other recent work is on [[self-assembly]] of [[amelogenin]] bio-[[macromolecules]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Wei | last2=Liu | first2=Ya | last3=Perez | first3=Toni | last4=Gunton | first4=J.D. | last5=Sorensen | first5=C.M. | last6=Chakrabarti | first6=A. | title=Kinetics of Nanochain Formation in a Simplified Model of Amelogenin Biomacromolecules | journal=Biophysical Journal | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=101 | issue=10 | year=2011 | issn=0006-3495 | doi=10.1016/j.bpj.2011.09.056 | pages=2502–2506| pmid=22098749 | pmc=3218329 | arxiv=1104.4970 | bibcode=2011BpJ...101.2502L }}</ref> [[Amelogenin]] is involved in the [[mineral]] [[deposition (geology)|deposition]] and has been postulated to fulfill major structural roles during highly organized ribbonlike [[carbonated]] [[apatite]] [[crystal formation]] in [[Vitreous enamel|enamel]] development, which is an unusual case in [[biomineralization]]. He also is working on [[fiber]] formation in [[sickle cell]] [[hemoglobin]], the mutant form of  hemoglobin  responsible for  sickle cell anemia .
